content.text: Last Updated On: 28th June 2025, 04:53 pm Thinking about making the District of Columbia your new home? Before choosing a moving company, it’s a great idea to understand the local climate. So, what is the weather like in Washington DC? Washington DC is an historic city with a population of just over 670,000, sitting on the Potomac River between Maryland and Virginia, and its inland location plays a major role in shaping its seasonal weather. The Washington DC climate is classified as humid subtropical under the Köppen-Trewartha system, with a zone code of Cfa. In this system, C stands for “mild temperature,” f means “fully humid,” and a indicates hot summers. So what does that actually mean for you? DC has four distinct seasons with hot, humid summers, cool and sometimes cold winters, and plenty of rain scattered throughout the year. The average temperature varies widely, so it’s important to know the Washington DC weather by month to pack and plan accordingly. Here’s a breakdown of the Washington DC climate. Climate vs. Weather Before we get into the details of the Washington DC climate, it’s helpful to understand the difference between climate and weather, two terms that are often used interchangeably but mean very different things. Understanding this distinction is key to interpreting Washington DC weather monthly trends and knowing what kind of temperatures, rainfall, and seasonal changes to expect throughout the year. According to the National Centers for Environmental Information, weather is the mix of events that happen every day in our atmosphere. Even though there’s only one atmosphere on Earth, Washington DC weather by month can vary just as much as it does across the globe. Weather includes daily highs and lows, the chance of rain, or whether you’ll need a coat tomorrow. It can change by the minute, hour, or day. Climate, on the other hand, refers to the average of those weather patterns over a long period (typically 30 years or more). So, when we talk about the climate of Washington DC or the climate in Washington DC, we’re talking about long-term patterns, not just what’s happening this week. Washington DC Seasons The Washington DC climate features four distinct seasons, giving residents a full range of seasonal experiences, from colorful autumns to hot, sunny summers. Spring and fall are often considered the most pleasant times of the year, with mild temperatures, blooming cherry blossoms in April, and fall foliage in October. Unlike some regions that experience a monsoon or wet/dry season pattern, Washington DC doesn’t have a defined rainy season. Rainfall is fairly evenly distributed throughout the year. DC is far enough inland that you don’t need to worry about hurricanes, but it can still feel the effects of hurricane seasons in the form of heavy rain and wind from tropical storms moving inland. Here’s a look at the different seasons in Washington DC. Spring in Washington DC Spring in Washington DC, spanning March, April, and May, is one of the most beautiful times of year. The Washington DC climate begins to warm, with blooming trees and flowers creating beautiful views across the city. The famous National Cherry Blossom Festival usually peaks in late March to April, drawing in thousands of visitors. As for the weather, the average temperature in Washington DC climbs from the 50s in March to the 70s by May. Spring is also one of the rainiest seasons in DC, so it’s smart to keep a raincoat or umbrella handy. The average rainfall is around 3 to 4 inches per month, contributing to the city’s annual average rainfall of 43.3 inches. Summer in Washington DC The months of June, July, and August are warm, sunny, and full of energy. The Washington DC climate in summer is marked by high humidity and soaring temperatures, often making it feel hotter than it is. The Washington DC summer temperature averages in the mid-80s, with July typically being the hottest month, seeing an average high temperature of around 88ªF. Thanks to the city’s proximity to the Atlantic Ocean, muggy air is common, and many locals search for ways to beat the heat and soak up the sunshine. You can visit public pools, kayak on the Potomac, or head to Rock Creek Park for a shaded hike. It’s also a great time to hire quality movers if you’re planning a summer relocation. Fall in Washington DC Autumn in Washington DC is often considered the best time to visit. During this season, the Washington DC climate is crisp and comfortable, with temperatures cooling from the 70s in September to the 50s by November. Humidity drops, and the city sees fewer crowds, making it perfect for exploring. Fall foliage is a major highlight, especially around the National Mall and Rock Creek Park. While rain is possible, it’s not excessive, averaging about 3 inches per month. Winter in Washington DC Winter brings chilly temperatures and seasonal fun. Does it snow in Washington DC? Yes, though snowfall can vary from year to year. The city averages about 14 inches of snow each year. The Washington DC winter weather is cold but manageable, with average temperatures in winter ranging from the mid-30s to the upper 40s. January is typically the coldest month, with average lows in the 20s. Still, there are plenty of things to do in Washington DC in winter. Enjoy Washington DC winter activities like ice skating at the National Gallery of Art’s Sculpture Garden, or check out the ZooLights display at the National Zoo. The Washington DC climate in winter may be brisk, but it offers a cozy, festive feel. Washington DC Weather by Month | Washington DC Average Temperatures Let’s break down the Washington DC climate month by month. Here’s a breakdown of the Washington DC weather by month and Washington DC temperature by month. January January is the coldest month, where the average temperature ranges from 30ºF (low) to an average high temperature of 44ºF. Expect freezing nights, occasional snowfall, and brisk winds near the Anacostia River, as the Washington DC climate is chilliest at this time. February February brings similar cold conditions. The average temperature ranges from 32ºF to 47ºF. It’s one of the snowiest months, with light precipitation and possible icy mornings. It’s a quiet time in the District of Columbia as tourism is at its lowest. March Spring arrives gradually, with average temperatures from 39ºF to 56ºF. Expect rain and rising humidity as the Washington DC climate begins to shift. Early cherry blossoms start blooming in parks across the city during this time. April With average temperatures from 48ºF to 67ºF, April is when DC begins to feel warm. It’s the peak of the National Cherry Blossom Festival. Precipitation increases slightly but is mostly rain, not snow. May May offers pleasant weather and average high temperatures near 75ºF and lows around 58ºF. It’s a popular time to visit outdoor attractions like those along the National Mall due to it being warm but not too hot. June Summer begins in June, and the Washington DC average temperature by month rises to 67ºF to 84ºF. It’s humid during this time, with plenty of sunshine and chances of rain. It’s a great time for the Smithsonian Folklife Festival and other city events. July This is the hottest month in the Washington DC climate calendar, with average temperatures ranging from 71ºF to 88ºF. High humidity makes it feel hotter than it is, making it a great time to hit the pool. Enjoy fun seasonal events like fireworks on the National Mall. August Still hot and humid, August sees average highs of 86ºF and lows of 70ºF. Expect frequent precipitation and summer storms. This time is popular for late summer tourists enjoying museum visits and summer strolls. September Temperatures begin to cool slightly during this time, ranging from 63ºF to 79ºF. Rain decreases, and humidity begins to drop. The Washington DC climate becomes more comfortable, making this a great time for outdoor festivals and early fall walks. October One of the best months for mild weather, with temperatures sitting between 51ºF and 68ºF. Cool, crisp air returns, and trees burst into color. This is the perfect time for a road trip around the city to enjoy the colorful leaves. November Average temperatures fall between 42ºF and 57ºF. Cold mornings and early darkness return, and you can expect light rain and perhaps some rare snowfall. During this time, you can expect fall festivals and Thanksgiving events across the District of Columbia. December Freezing returns with average temperatures between 34ºF and 48ºF. One of the cooler months in the Washington DC weather by month overview, with light snow and holiday events lighting up the city. Annual Washington DC Climate Statistics In order to better understand the Washington DC climate and the Washington DC weather year round, you’ll want to take a look at a few Washington DC weather averages. Summers are hot and humid, with dew point levels often making the air feel even more oppressive. The Washington Post recently reported that the Washington DC area should brace for one of the hottest summers in history. Although DC is not in Tornado Alley, thunderstorms are common in the warmer months, sometimes bringing tornado warnings and flash flooding. Climate change is also influencing the Washington DC climate, making extreme weather more frequent and intense. What used to be rare precipitation events could become regular occurrences, and rising sea levels and stronger storms are long-term concerns, particularly for low-lying areas. Best Time to Visit Washington DC The Washington DC climate makes spring (March to May) the best time to visit, thanks to mild temperatures and the famous cherry blossoms in full bloom. Early fall (September to October) is another favorite, offering comfortable weather and beautiful autumn leaves. Visitors typically avoid July, the hottest and most humid month, with average highs near 88ºF. However, the summer months do bring plenty of outdoor activities and farmer’s markets, so if you can brave the heat, it’s worth the trip.
